newsitem.title: UK: Flamboyant British ex-minister heads for safe seat.
newsitem.headline: Flamboyant British ex-minister heads for safe seat.

text.p: Self-confessed philanderer and former defence minister Alan Clark is to return to the political fray after being chosen as an election candidate for one of the safest Conservative seats in Britain.
The raffish Clark, who once made a speech to parliament as a minister when "not entirely sober", freely admitted in his best-selling diaries to a string of sexual conquests.

Alleged to have seduced the wife of a judge and then had affairs with her two daughters, Clark promised on landing the safe Kensington and Chelsea nomination for the forthcoming election he would behave "in a proper and suitable fashion".

He won a tight contest on Thursday night that went to three ballots and will replace Sir Nicholas Scott, who was dropped after being found lying face down in the street when attending a reception during the Conservative Party conference.

Clark, a devoted admirer of former premier Margaret Thatcher, said he always regretted quitting parliament before the last election in 1992. He has now landed a safe, affluent seat within striking distance of the House of Commons.
Prime Minister John Major must call the election by May 22 at the latest.

He made no secret of his fierce loyalty to Thatcher, dumped as prime minister by her Conservative colleagues in 1990. Clark said he found her attractive but then the notorious lady's man added swiftly: "I didn't want to jump on her."

After his remarkable comeback the 68-year-old maverick, who lives in an inherited family castle in southern England, said he did not think he would be as colourful as before but then added: "I am never flamboyant on purpose. I am what I am."
